0.long_answer: Lorna Wing was a British psychiatrist whose work in autism research significantly influenced the field. In 1976, she coined the term 'Asperger's syndrome,' a term that would go on to be widely used to describe a particular set of autism-related symptoms. In addition to introducing this term, Wing played a crucial role in establishing the National Autistic Society in the UK, which was one of the first organisations aimed at supporting people with autism and their families. Her contributions helped shape contemporary understanding and advocacy for autism.
